text:
olivia: Heads-up — after the RBAC tighten PR landed in prod this morning, several interservice mTLS handshakes are failing in eu-west. Seen 502s and TLS alerts.
raj: Which services? any pattern (ingress vs east-west)?
olivia: Reporter list: user-frontend -> authsvc, billing-worker -> kv-store, metrics-collector -> ingest-proxy. All on eu-west. Northamerica looks fine.
maya: I pulled a sample from authsvc logs: `tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate`. KMS unwrap logs show: `AccessDenied` for the ephemeral-keystore role.
liam: security-bot just emitted an alert too — looks like the RBAC change removed `kms:Decrypt` for the `service:ephemeral-rotator` principal in the eu key policy.
security-bot: Alert: KMS Unwrap failures detected (eu-west-1). 28 errors in 5m. CLI query: `aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/ephemeral-keystore` returned missing grant for `service:ephemeral-rotator`.
aaron: Is this the same RBAC PR that tightened iam:AssumeRole mappings? If so, devops might have removed a legacy ARN allowance.
maya: Yep — PR #4923 modified role bindings to narrow scope. It unintentionally removed the cross-account service principal used by the rotator.
liam: Short-term mitigation: rebind temporary grant so KMS unwraps succeed and can re-issue certs. Proposed command (audit-first):
```
# create grant for rotator principal
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/ephemeral-keystore --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/service-ephemeral-rotator --operations Decrypt --retiring-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/robot-ops
```
raj: Can we scope it to eu-west only? Also add an expiry TTL (grant tokens will expire on key rotation), include auditor mention.
olivia: Agreed. Liam, can you run a canary grant in eu-west for 15m and monitor? I'll pause the RBAC rollout until we confirm.
liam: Will do. Creating grant now with note `temp-canary-ephemeral-unwrap` and 15m monitor.
security-bot: FYI — after grant creation, authsvc TLS handshakes recovered for two nodes. 502 count dropped to 3.
maya: Next step: update the RBAC PR to explicitly include the KMS grant creation as a change in the rollout checklist (or add a post-merge job to ensure grants exist). We also need an automated audit rule that flags KMS unwrap denies.
aaron: Also add an integration test: run `kubectl -n authsvc exec` -> trigger cert rotation -> assert KMS unwrap success. We should run this in eu and na in CI.
olivia: Good catch on monitoring. For long-term, product question: should we consolidate ephemeral keys to one cross-region principal or create region-scoped principals? Thoughts?
raj: Prefer region-scoped principals to limit blast radius and to align with our keystore replication model. But we need automation to avoid drift during RBAC changes.
liam: I can add a terraform module to manage KMS grants tied to role IDs and include it in the RBAC pipeline so grants are updated atomically.
maya: Also file a vuln/incident doc referencing the RBAC PR and KMS grant issue. I'll create INCIDENT-2026-04-kms-rbac-unwrap and link it here.
olivia: Assign owners: liam = mitigation + terraform module, maya = incident doc + audit rule, raj = RBAC rollout gating and CI test, aaron = oncall followups.
liam: Running the canary grant now. Will post results in 10m.
security-bot: Postmortem task created: PM-12345. Reminder: add `kms:DescribeKey` audits to our logshipper so denies are visible in Splunk.
olivia: Thanks everyone. Once canary finishes clean, we'll patch the RBAC PR with the grant step and continue rollout with a stricter pre-merge check. :thumbsup:
